case.court: United States Court of Appeals for the Ninth Circuit
case.limits: The court decided standing, not the outer definition of authorship, and it addressed an animal rather than a system a human directs. It answers who cannot own a work, not who does.
case.holding: A crested macaque that took photographs of itself lacked statutory standing under the Copyright Act, because the Act's terms presume human authors and next-of-kin, and a non-human cannot sue for infringement of works it created.

live_cases.name: University of Tennessee Research Foundation v. Anthropic PBC

case.why_ai_cites_it: The monkey-selfie case is the closest appellate authority that a non-human creator has no rights in what it makes. It is cited to establish that model outputs have no author of their own, which cuts for AI companies when they disclaim ownership and against anyone trying to anchor rights in the machine itself.
